Award Contract No. WW-748, As-Needed Spot Sewer Replacement No. 45, to the responsible bidder that submitted the lowest responsive bid, J. Flores Construction Company, Inc., in the amount of $9,881,978, with a duration of 400 consecutive calendar days, to replace sections of existing sewer pipe on an as-needed basis at locations that staff will determine throughout the City and County of San Francisco. Ryan Freeborn, Project Manager, and Katie Miller, Director of Water Capital Projects, responded to a question from Commissioner Maxwell regarding items 6d and 6e and the use of earthquake pipes for the contract listed under item 6e but not for the contract listed under item 6d. Director Miller added that installation of Kubota earthquake resistant pipe was an intentional pilot project for the contract under item 6e due to the proximity of the pipe to San Francisco General Hospital. She stated the cost and added value will be evaluated by staff for potential future projects. Vice President Rivera discussed his previous work with the Japanese manufacturer of the Kubota pipe and noted the flexibility of the pipe during a seismic event
Public Hearing to consider and possible action to approve the scope, schedule, and budget of the March 2024 Proposed Revised Water System Improvement Program
items.text: Public Hearing to consider and possible action to approve the scope, schedule, and budget of the March 2024 Proposed Revised Water System Improvement Program; and direct staff to send a Notice of Change Report to the State Water Resources Control Board and the Alfred E. Alquist Seismic Safety Commission in compliance with California Water Code Section 73500, et seq. Director Miller requested approval of the scope, schedule, and budget for the March 2024 Proposed revised Water System Improvement Program, and for direction to send a Notice of Change Report to the State Water Resources Control Board and the Alfred E. Alquist Seismic Safety Commission, in compliance with the California Water Code. She stated the program is 99% complete with three active projects remaining. She indicated the program was last revised in 2022 with three projects completed since that time. She discussed refinements and changes that are needed to the Regional Groundwater and Storage Recovery Project and the Alameda Creek Recapture Project. Director Miller indicated that staff have met with Bay Area Water and Supply Conservation Agency (BAWSCA) staff to discuss the proposed changes and noted BAWSCA’s comments that were provided to staff and the Commission. She indicated staff generally concur with BAWSCA’s comments, including comments that another Notice of Change will be necessary in the future due to the potential additional changes to the Alameda Creek Recapture Project

items.title: Public Hearing to consider and approve the Water Miscellaneous Fee schedule
items.text: Public Hearing to consider and approve the Water Miscellaneous Fee schedule, which includes the revision of existing fees, elimination of certain fees, and adoption of new fees and charges related to the provision of water service within and outside the City and County of San Francisco. If approved, the proposed fees will become effective July 1, 2024 and will remain effective until revised. This action constitutes the Approval Action for the Project for the purposes of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), pursuant to San Francisco Administrative Code section 31.04(h). The Planning Department has determined that the Project is exempt from the CEQA. The Commission will rely on that determination to make its decision on this action

items.title: Public Hearing to consider and approve the Wastewater Miscellaneous Fee schedule, which includes the revision of existing fees
items.text: Public Hearing to consider and approve the Wastewater Miscellaneous Fee schedule, which includes the revision of existing fees and the adoption of new fees and charges related to the provision of sewer services within the City and County of San Francisco. If approved, the proposed fees will become effective July 1, 2024, and will remain effective until revised. This action constitutes the Approval Action for the Project for the purposes of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), pursuant to San Francisco Administrative Code section 31.04(h). The Planning Department has determined that the Project is exempt from the CEQA. The Commission will rely on that determination to make its decision on this action. Kristin Avenis, Rates Analyst, provided an overview of miscellaneous fees, indicating charges are for individual customers for optional services or as penalties and deposits. Revenues received reduce the need to increase retail rates, enhancing equity for rate payers. Analyst Avenis discussed the miscellaneous fee study schedule which began in 2023 and will conclude in July 2024 with the adoption of the proposed miscellaneous fees. She provided definition of miscellaneous fee methodology which consists of (1) Cost of providing service (labor, overhead, and materials and equipment); (2) Policy screening (affordability considerations and penalties to incentivize compliance); and (3) Staff review (coordination with department managers, and executive review). items.title: Approve the terms and conditions and authorize the General Manager to execute a Purchase and Sale Agreement and Easement Deed with San Mateo County Flood and Sea Level Rise Resiliency District
items.text: Approve the terms and conditions and authorize the General Manager to execute a Purchase and Sale Agreement and Easement Deed with San Mateo County Flood and Sea Level Rise Resiliency District for the acquisition of a 1,386-square-foot easement for an aerial water pipeline crossing and associated footings and braces across a portion of San Mateo County Assessor’s Parcel No. 011-322-200 for $70,000, subject to Board of Supervisors’ and Mayor’s approval. Dina Brasil, Right-of-Way Manager, Real Estate Services, reviewed the Groundwater Phase 2B project, which will install a groundwater pump at the South San Francisco Main well site and an 8-inch pipeline within El Camino Real and Chestnut Avenue to transport groundwater to Cal Water’s groundwater treatment plant. She discussed the needs for the easements and the status of negotiations for each site. Manager Brasil noted an error on the third Whereas Clause in the resolution that inadvertently indicate the installation of a 12-inch diameter groundwater pipeline, stating the installation is for an 8-inch diameter groundwater pipeline. Manager Brasil reviewed the transaction details and noted a purchase price of $70,000 (equal to the appraised value) and additional regular closing costs. In response to a question from Commissioner Maxwell, Steve Ritchie, Assistant General Manager (AGM), Water Enterprise, discussed the decision-making process for placement of groundwater pumps

items.title: Approve modification of the Green Infrastructure Grant Program Guidelines to raise the maximum cost per acre of impervious surface area managed by grant-funded projects
items.text: Approve modification of the Green Infrastructure Grant Program Guidelines to raise the maximum cost per acre of impervious surface area managed by grant-funded projects from $930,000 to $1,035,000 and the maximum grant award per project from $2,000,000 to $2,500,000 to account for inflation; revise funding disbursement requirements for City Departments only; and revise program eligibility criteria and other program requirements. Sarah Bloom, Senior Watershed Planner indicated since the program began in 2019, there have been 22 grants awarded totaling just over $23 million, with five of the projects completed construction and the remaining in planning and design phases. She indicated the proposed modifications represent a collection of lessons-learned and are aimed at gaining efficiencies and maximizing program benefits. She highlighted substantial changes (1) increase the maximum cost per acre that the program awards from $930,000 to $1,035,000 per acre to account for inflation and to allow for full cost of design and construction of Green Infrastructure facilities; (2) increase per project maximum grant award from $2 million to $2.5 million to continue to award projects of a similar size as the cost per acre increases; (3) allow grantees to request grant amendment for additional funding if through the planning and design process it is discovered the project can handle manage additional stormwater performance; (4) expand definition of eligible projects to include projects tha
